title: Reflecting in the Reflection: Integrating a Socratic Questioning Framework into Automated AI-Based Question Generation
extended_summary:
This preprint addresses the challenge of designing high-quality reflection questions for education. The authors argue that reflection prompts are important for metacognition and deeper learning, but they are time-consuming to create and often uneven in quality. Prior automated question generation work has focused mostly on factual recall or closed-ended item types, leaving a gap for reflective, open-ended prompts that are pedagogically grounded.

To address this gap, the paper proposes a reflection-in-reflection framework that uses two role-specialized LLM agents: a Student–Teacher agent that drafts a reflection question and a Teacher–Educator agent that responds with Socratic coaching questions to iteratively refine it. The system takes as input a topic, key concepts, optional student level information, and optional instructional materials. It is designed to support iterative revision, explicit rationales, and adaptive stopping when the question is judged satisfactory.

The paper evaluates the framework in an authentic lower-secondary ICT context using instructional materials for 8th–9th grade students in Czechia, focusing on internet fundamentals such as servers, routers, packets, and decentralization. However, the evaluation is performed on generated questions using a stronger LLM as evaluator rather than on teachers or students using the system in practice. The main findings are that dynamic stopping and contextual information improve question quality, and that the two-agent Socratic protocol produces questions judged more relevant and deeper than a one-shot baseline. The authors conclude that structured Socratic prompting can improve AI-generated reflective questions and may help educators author better prompts more efficiently.

identified_tools.name: ChatGPT
identified_tools.description: OpenAI GPT-family large language model used here as the backbone model for two LLM-based agents (Student–Teacher and Teacher–Educator) and as the external GPT-4-class evaluator.
identified_tools.use_case: Used to generate reflection questions through a two-agent Socratic dialogue (GPT-4o-mini backbone) and to evaluate outputs with a stronger GPT-4-class model in pairwise comparisons.

findings.finding_summary: The paper reports that the two-agent reflection-in-reflection protocol using a GPT-4o-mini backbone outperformed a one-shot GPT-4o-mini baseline on generated question quality. Across context settings, the protocol was judged better for relevance (gamma ranging from 0.60 to 0.92) and generally better for depth (average above 0.6, with values such as gamma(depth)=0.77 and 0.91 in underspecified conditions), while clarity and overall quality were also usually slightly above 0.5 but with smaller gains.
findings.measure: Pairwise LLM-evaluated clarity, relevance, depth, and overall quality of generated reflection questions
findings.effect_size: gamma ranges: relevance 0.60-0.92; depth average >0.6; clarity around 0.50-0.64 in most conditions; overall quality around 0.50-0.58 in most conditions

quality_tier_rationale: This is a preprint describing an empirical comparison, but the evaluation relies on LLM-based pairwise judgments rather than human-rated or experimental classroom outcomes, and sample sizes/effect estimates are not fully reported. The design is informative but not strong enough for blue/green evidence.
impact_tier_rationale: The reported preference indices show modest-to-substantial advantages over the one-shot baseline, especially for relevance and depth, with gamma values often well above 0.20 above chance. However, the evidence is about generated-question quality rather than direct teacher uptake or learning impact.
